authority.tenantAuthority: Knowledge sources, documents, chunks, vectors, jobs, chat sessions and messages are tenant-scoped domain rows. Only a current ACTIVE membership resolves tenant authority; a browser-supplied organization identifier is never authority.
authority.storageAuthority: Object bytes live in a private storage bucket under tenant-derived object keys. A signed operation is issued only after server-side tenant/resource checks and is short-lived and single-purpose.
authority.retrievalAuthority: Authorization predicates run inside both lexical and vector retrieval before candidates leave storage, and are rechecked again before context assembly. An unauthorized candidate reaching provider context is a STOP.
authority.chatAuthority: Sessions and messages are owned by tenant plus subject. Every history, export, resume, regenerate and source-open path reauthorizes current membership and source access.
authority.providerAuthority: The provider receives only minimal authorized context. Prompts, source text and raw provider output are denied at default log, trace and metric ingestion; a non-default raw sink requires an accepted R3 decision.

rules: Every operation maps to exactly one of knowledge.manage or knowledge.read from the M2-C01 permission matrix.
Retrieval and chat paths require knowledge.read; ingestion, deletion and reindex paths require knowledge.manage.
The effective permission is evaluated on fresh ACTIVE membership plus the frozen M2 role matrix; stale membership denies.

authority.honestyBoundary: All retention values, limits, defaults and provisional identifiers (including the tbd revision placeholder and runtime-verified model ids) in this contract are accepted v0.1 planning defaults, not current runtime behavior or production evidence. No production-retention or compliance claim is made by this artifact.

rules: organizationId is server-derived from the resolved tenant context, never from the request body.
Deletion sets DELETED and makes every contained document retrieval-ineligible before cleanup completes.
A DELETED knowledge base rejects new documents and new retrieval eligibility.
name is bounded 1..200 characters; description is bounded 0..2000 characters.

deduplication.rule: A duplicate upload for an existing non-DELETED document with the same digest is idempotent and returns the existing record instead of creating a second one.

rules: The stored object key is derived from organizationId + knowledgeBaseId + documentId; path guessing never grants access.
MIME is sniffed from bytes and must match the accepted format; the client filename and its extension are never trusted.
sha256 is computed server-side over the raw bytes and stored for provenance and deduplication.
Deletion makes the document retrieval-ineligible first (state DELETED), then propagates per the lifecycle.deletionOrder planes with a durable receipt.
A FAILED document can never become partially searchable as READY.
The job row and the document row transition in the same database transaction wherever the state moves.
Claim uses bounded lease semantics; a crashed worker's lease expires and the job becomes claimable again.
Cancellation is idempotent and only valid from QUEUED or RUNNING.
Job progress is read from the durable API; Realtime only shortens perceived latency.
Attempts are bounded; the last safe error code is stored without stack traces or secrets.
Chunking is deterministic for identical input bytes and strategy version.
Every chunk records source page range and section provenance.
The token budget is counted by the implementation-owned tokenizer and pinned in the strategy version; the tokenizer choice is an M4-T02/T03 implementation decision, not this contract.
A strategy version change requires a full versioned reindex; old chunks are superseded, never mutated in place.
chunk.text is never logged or placed in default traces.
A superseded or deleted chunk is never retrieval-eligible.
Document deletion marks every chunk DELETED before vector cleanup.
The model id, revision and dimensions are stored on every vector row.
revision must be a concrete immutable digest or version recorded by M4-T03; a label or task pointer is never a valid stored value.
A dimension mismatch between query and stored vectors is rejected, not silently padded.
A model or revision change uses a new storage partition or a complete versioned reindex.
The embedding adapter has explicit timeout, concurrency, token and cost bounds.
Vector queries apply the same tenant and permission predicates as lexical retrieval before candidate output.
Source deletion removes future vector eligibility immediately and physical cleanup follows the documented job.
No provider secret or raw document body enters logs or traces.

predicate.definition: organizationId equals the resolved tenant context AND chunk.state in retrievalEligibleStates AND document.state in retrievalEligibleStates AND the resolved membership holds knowledge.read per the M2-C01 matrix
rules: The same predicate expression is applied by the lexical adapter, the vector adapter and the fused result set.
The predicate runs inside the storage query wherever possible; the post-query recheck before context assembly uses the identical expression.
Lexical and vector adapters emit the same normalized result object.
Ranking is deterministic for the same corpus, query and configuration.
Context assembly truncates deterministically when the token budget is reached and records the truncated candidate count.
The budget is configuration-visible and bounded; it never admits a candidate beyond the authorized set.

fusion.tuningOwnership: M4-T04 owns the exact top-K and candidate values as bounded configuration; this contract freezes only the algorithm, version and bounds, not the tuned numbers.
rules: Top-K and candidate limits are bounded and configuration-visible.
One branch unavailable degrades to the other branch without weakening authorization.
Both branches empty produces an honest no-match result.
The evaluation corpus has a pinned checksum and version.
Metrics are reported against the versioned corpus only; hand-picked examples are never a claim.
Sessions are owned by tenant plus subject; every read, write, export and delete reauthorizes that ownership.
Deletion propagates to messages, retrieval-run links, feedback and provider-side state Nexora controls.
Default retention is 90 days for completed sessions; canceled or failed drafts are diagnostic-retained for 7 days.
A streaming, canceled or failed assistant draft is never labeled COMPLETED.
Regenerate creates a new revision linked through parentMessageId; the prior revision is preserved.
Sending is idempotent via clientMessageId scoped to session plus subject; a duplicate send returns the existing message.

clientMessageId is bounded printable input; clientMessageIdDigest is sha256:<64 lowercase hex> computed over the exact UTF-8 bytes of clientMessageId and is the persisted deduplication key. The raw clientMessageId is never logged or placed in traces.
Pagination uses stable cursors; deleted messages disappear from history after propagation.
Every displayed citation resolves to an authorized chunk and document at access time.
A citation whose source lost access shows an unavailable-source state, never the content.
Historical citations are reauthorized when opened.
Cancellation propagates to the provider request and persists the CANCELLED state.
Timeouts are bounded and produce a visible partial-failure state.
No provider secret or raw source text appears in the stream metadata.
The deterministic CI provider is used for all automated tests; live provider smoke is separate and labeled with model, version and date.
Provider output is untrusted data and never higher-priority instructions.
No-answer or low-confidence queries return an honest no-answer state.
Low-confidence is defined by the fused retrieval outcome: an empty candidate set, or a best fused score below the accepted no-answer threshold recorded by M4-T05, triggers NO_ANSWER.
Export reauthorizes current membership and source access at collection time.
The export artifact is encrypted, short-lived (24h) and purged after expiry.
Excluded categories are recorded with reasons in the manifest.
Traces record safe IDs, hashes, counts and outcomes only.
Raw prompt, context and source text are disabled from default traces.
Retention is 30 days for redacted metadata; aggregate quality metrics may live 180 days.
Trace inspection requires tenant admin authorization and is cross-tenant denied.

deletionOrder: cancel or terminalize any in-flight documentJob for the document
mark vectors DELETED and remove lexical/vector index entries
chatDeletionOrder: tombstone session (deletedAt) and make history retrieval-ineligible
rules: A deleted source can never remain retrievable while cleanup is pending.
Every read path predicates on eligible states, so a marked row can never be served while physical cleanup is pending.
Deletion is idempotent and resumable; partial completion is never labeled success.
Cross-tenant deletion or export is a STOP.

securityInvariants: Authorization filters run during retrieval and are rechecked before context assembly.
Unauthorized candidates or context reaching provider construction is a STOP.
Sources are untrusted data and never higher-priority instructions.
Raw prompts, source text and secrets are denied at default log, trace and metric ingestion; a non-default raw sink requires an accepted R3 decision.
Session and message ownership is tenant plus subject scoped and reauthorized on every access path.
A streaming, canceled or failed assistant draft is never labeled completed.
